A crowded short (23.8% of shares, highest of 23 settlements) plus a call that can restate ERCOT status leans up. findings.finding: The print is management's first statement since the 2026-11-03 Texas governor result. Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned for an immediate moratorium on new data centers, won. CORZ fell 10.25% on 11-04 (Cipher -17%, IREN about -4% to -12%). CORZ's own 2026-09-10 8-K says Denton's 297 MW (CoreWeave) is ERCOT-approved and NOT subject to Batch Zero, with +74 MW also outside it. Pecos 300+300 MW and Hunt 431 MW are conditionally approved in Batch Zero as Base Load, and Hunt construction has commenced with collateral posted. Cantor's note on the same day says it still expects conditional baseload projects to proceed, and Hinojosa takes office 2027-01-19. The call can restate this status. Against that: two of the five AMD sites (Pecos, Hunt) are in Texas and Dalton is in Georgia, where Goldman also expects a conditional moratorium.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print after a policy shock. The 2026-07-28 print announced a $14B AMD deal and a revenue beat and closed +0.02% (baseline), so good strategic news has not been paid on print day. Peer read on 11-04: Riot, with existing approvals, was described as insulated while Cipher's unapproved pipeline fell 17% (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cipher-mining-sinks-17-as-texas-election-puts-ai-datacenter-expansion-at-risk-4999248).
findings.why_not_priced: The election result is one session old, and the market sold every Texas-exposed name together. Cipher's -17% and CORZ's -10% do not distinguish approved Base Load capacity from pipeline capacity. If the market had separated CORZ's ERCOT status, CORZ would have fallen like Riot (described as insulated) rather than near Cipher. The CNBC, Investing and Fool coverage of the day does not mention CORZ at all.
findings.independence: Cantor (via Investing.com, 2026-11-04) expects conditional baseload projects to proceed: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cipher-mining-sinks-17-as-texas-election-puts-ai-datacenter-expansion-at-risk-4999248. Counterpoint from a different source: Bernstein on 2026-08-04 named CORZ among the names most sensitive to timeline pressure from moratoria on new capacity (https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/bernstein-texas-power-grid-moratorium-may-not-affect-btc-miners-materially), and Goldman expects conditional moratoria in TX, GA and MI (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/04/data-center-stocks-just-plunged-after-the-midterms-is-it-time-to-buy-the-dip/). Election facts: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/ai-stocks-texas-governor-data-centers.html

findings.finding: Crowded short into a bmo print at the 52-week low. FINRA short interest was 76.6M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 23.8% of shares outstanding, 5.16 days to cover, up 10.6M and the highest of 23 settlements. The stock closed 11-04 at $12.78, 3.8% above its $12.31 52-week low, after a -10.25% day. Any reassuring line on Texas status, AMD financing or a new lease meets a short base that added into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not cover this name squeezing on a print. Its last two misses (2026-03-02 -7.22%, 2026-05-06 -9.22%) were not cushioned by shorts, and short interest was about 19.6% of float in August (snippet, equibles), lower than now.
findings.why_not_priced: The +9.99 put skew and the -10% day show the market positioned for downside, not for a cover. If a squeeze were priced, the skew would be flat or call-bid and the stock would not be sitting on its 52-week low into the print.
findings.independence: SwingTradeBot shows 27% of float and 6.28 days to cover (https://swingtradebot.com/equities/CORZ), from the same FINRA data, so this is not independent. The skew and price come from the sealed baseline and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CORZ/.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is largely fixed by the company's own July disclosure. It was billing 437 MW in mid-July, about $635M of annualised GAAP colocation revenue, or roughly $159M a quarter. Q2 colocation was $136.7M and Q2 total revenue $164.2M. Self-mining is winding down (Q2 $21.5M at a -56% gross margin), so Q3 total comes to about $180M. That is a beat against Earnings Whispers' $172.6M and a miss against FXEmpire's $198.4M from 10 analysts. Adj. EBITDA should rise mechanically from Q2's $41.1M as low-margin mining shrinks. The figure sits inside what management told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue beat (164.2M vs ~145M) and the stock closed +0.02%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-02): revenue miss plus no new customer, -7.22%. Q1 2026: -9.22%. Revenue beats have not been paid and misses have been punished. Peer Cipher fell about 5% on a Q3 revenue miss on 2026-11-02 (Yahoo news list).
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the billing figure is public. The consensus gap ($172.6M vs $198.4M) means part of the street models more MW or pass-through revenue than the 437 MW disclosure supports. That high end is where a headline 'miss' would come from.
findings.independence: The MarketBeat call summary has the CFO's 'meaningful step-up' and the fact that Dalton Phase II (150 MW) only starts at end-2026: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-core-scientific-inc-stock/. Both rest on the same company disclosure.

findings.finding: Billing growth pauses until Dalton Phase II. Per the Q2 call, CoreWeave's 590 MW is the contracted total, of which about 437 MW was billing in July, and the last 150 MW (Dalton Phase II) starts at end-2026 and completes in early 2027. The first AMD megawatts come in H1 2027 at Pecos. Q4 colocation is therefore roughly flat on Q3. Management said it hoped to bring a new site to market 'by year-end' and hired a Chief Commercial Officer on 2026-09-25. A Q4 outlook without a new lease looks like a stall; a new signing would break it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-03-02: the CEO admitted missing a self-imposed goal of signing a new customer before the call, and the stock fell 7.22% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/core-scientific-stock-plunges-7-2-on-earnings-miss-why-a-27-target-is-next). 2026-07-28: the AMD signing was announced at the print and the stock closed flat.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's $198M consensus suggests some models still carry growth. A flat Q4 outlook with no new tenant would show the step-up story pausing for two quarters, at the moment the Texas result makes new Texas leases harder to sign. If this were priced, consensus would cluster near the ~$180M the billing supports.
findings.independence: The CCO appointment is from the company newsroom (https://corescientific.com/resources/newsroom/, 2026-09-25). The newsroom shows no lease announcement since the August Polaris DS deal. Weak, same company.

findings.finding: CoreWeave, the customer behind essentially all colocation revenue (590 MW contracted), is in credit stress. Its 2030-2032 notes were implied at 15-16% yields, CDS implied about 60% five-year default probability, and the stock fell nearly 25% in the week to about 2026-10-16 (Crypto Briefing, 2026-10-25). CoreWeave's own Q3 is on 2026-11-10, outside the window. On CORZ's call this becomes counterparty and receivables questioning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2025 a CoreWeave guidance cut tied to a data-center developer's delays took CORZ down about 7% (https://whale-alert.io/stories/c05cb22c150f/CoreWeave-warns-data-center-developer-delays-will-hit-Q4-cuts-full-year-outlook-shares-fall-9-pre-market-after-Core-Scientific-deal-rejection). No CORZ print reaction on this line exists.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CORZ fell 17% in October. The article does not name CORZ, and the CORZ-specific exposure (single-tenant revenue, 12-year straight-line leases) is a second-order read. It is shrunk because the short base is crowded.
findings.independence: The CoreWeave Q3 date (2026-11-10) is at https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Announces-Date-of-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-and-Conference-Call/default.aspx. This is a proxy: CORZ has not confirmed any payment issue.

findings.finding: Funding the AMD build: about $6B of capex for 530 MW at $11-12M/MW, to be financed mainly with project-level SPV bonds. A $600M senior secured facility was added on 2026-08-27. Q2 long-term debt was $4.30B and liquidity $1.82B. What the money buys is real: 15-year AMD agreements with more than $14B of base contracted revenue. The risk in the window is financing terms (cost, or equity or convert issuance at a $12.78 stock) disclosed with the print, now that two of five AMD sites sit in Texas.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print-day financing reaction in the baseline. On 2026-03-27 the stock fell 4.15% as the funding-driven pivot came into focus with bitcoin weakness (https://rallies.ai/news/core-scientific-slides-as-bitcoin-weakens-and-funding-driven-ai-pivot-stays-in-focus).
findings.why_not_priced: The Texas result is one day old, and the cost of SPV bonds for Texas sites has not been reset in any public number. An equity raise at the 52-week low is not in any preview. The money funds contracted demand (lesson 4), so the sign is only mildly negative.
findings.independence: The capex per MW and SPV plan come from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-core-scientific-inc-stock/). Debt and liquidity come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839341/000183934126000013/q22026corescientificinc-ea.htm).

findings.finding: A large non-cash warrant/CVR gain will make GAAP EPS hugely positive against a -$0.03 consensus. In Q2 a stock rise to $25.60 (June close) produced a $1,045.5M fair-value LOSS. The stock closed September at $15.98 (-37.6% in the quarter), so most of that should reverse as a gain in Q3. Headline EPS would show a 'beat' with no operating content.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a -$3.32 GAAP EPS against a -$0.06 consensus, driven by the same line, closed +0.02%. The market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus EPS of -$0.03 ignores the mark. It is below operating income with no path to guidance, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: The Q2 warrant/CVR loss of $1,045.5M is in the Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839341/000183934126000013/q22026corescientificinc-ea.htm

baseline_tension: The two positive findings (Texas status clarification, crowded short) cut against the +10 put skew and the -19% 20-day run-up. The negatives (CoreWeave credit, growth pause, financing) agree with the skew. The net is a small positive lean held near 50 because of the skew.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): the Texas-status finding was cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because a reassurance on a call is an argument about reaction, not a document the option market has missed.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): CoreWeave credit -0.5 to -0.4 and growth-pause guidance -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money funds 15-year AMD contracts with >$14B of revenue, so the financing finding moved from -0.5 to -0.2.
Lesson 2 (one-offs at a fraction): the warrant/CVR gain moved from +0.3 to +0.2, since Q2's same line was looked through.
Lesson 5 (proxy small): the Cipher peer read moved from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 6 (disputed bar): the reported-quarter finding stays capped at -0.2.
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 10 to 11. p_up unchanged at 52.
Net: the findings sum is unchanged at +0.8 because the cuts offset; expected_move moved from 0.40 to 0.44 on the abs_move change.
